rv.q: The warmth generated by the pair fills the Troubadour’s rather daunting space and their voices blend beautifully, diffusing the memory of the brash, boisterous opening numbers and continual scene-setting.
Even the most casual viewers will find something to love in this visually enthralling production.

While some may roll their eyes at the bubblegum trilogy, many people were devouring the sappy storylines and bopping (to the top) with the earworms – a formula that translates as perfectly on stage as it did on the screen.
Shamelessly bland music ranges from amusement arcade jingles, to hyperglycaemic schmaltz, mixed with militant cheerleading and tai-chi choreography, run fast or slow as the mood requires.
No, it can't escape the limitations of the story's spectacularly two-dimensional characters... but it's bright and buzzy nonetheless.
This is a show that will surely Bop to the Top of theatre ratings, because it’s impossible not to leave the theatre grinning from ear to ear.
Electric, heart-racing and magnificently entertaining, this revival brings a beloved classic back to life with considerable flair.
This inventive approach brings a fresh interactive dimension to the familiar story, combining catchy songs with dynamic choreography and imaginative use of space.
Twenty years after its premiere on Disney Channel, the Millennial staple hits the stage in a charming, energetic production.
There's nothing wrong with harmless fun in a production that is indeed, as one of its lyrics puts it, 'soarin'' and 'flyin'' – with enthusiasm and exuberance.
Theatre is an ecosystem, and High School Musical fulfils its role immaculately and with significant flair.
The result is an absolute slam dunk, capturing everything audiences loved about the original while finding fresh energy of its own.
This production is sure to entertain Wildcats young and old in one of the most fun shows I have seen in some time.
It’s simply a fun, feel-good stage adaptation that gives fans another chance to enjoy the songs and characters they grew up with.
If you want a nostalgic night out, an opportunity to revisit some familiar songs and a show that doesn't take itself too seriously, High School Musical is worth a visit.
This stage adaptation offers audiences the chance to relive those memories together.
If you are not already smitten with the movie franchise, there is plenty of fast paced action but the plot and characterisation seem strictly 2D.
As a theatre production, I feel it has misplaced energy and a lack of character conviction from many of the cast.

You could genuinely revitalise me from a coma with the opening notes of I've Had the Time of My Life or the first bars of Don't You (Forget About Me). So, naturally, High School Musical is right up my street. This is feel-good theatre with the stakes pleasingly low.
This is undeniably a brilliant production with a sincere message at its heart.
A simple story, beautifully told and flawlessly performed. Take your teens (or your teenage selves), grab some popcorn and go see this slam-dunk of a show.
Exhilarating choreography and full-out musical numbers ensure that High School Musical at Troubadour Wembley Park Theatre is hugely enjoyable for audiences of all ages.
Familiar but fresh, low stakes and high energy, this will bop to the top as exactly what fans have been looking for.
The level of care that has gone into the show reflects in every moment, if nothing else.
The infectious energy, beloved songs and enthusiastic performances ensure audiences will have a great time.
A fair effort to adapt an inimitable phenomena that ultimately proves unsuccessful.

cn.t: Critics praise this energetic, nostalgia-fueled production for its immersive staging and infectious spirit, though some find the material thin. The spectacle and audience participation delight, but substance occasionally takes a backseat to feel-good fun.

vr.q: It is a great time at the theater and they have spared no expense, both in terms of actual expense and in terms of real care and passion in bringing this to the stage.
